CE credits available for Ontario advisors who are licensed.Gender Differences in Benefit Plans: Diagnosis, Treatment and Outcomes
March 5, 2026, 8:00am – 12:00pm Eastern
(8:00am – 8:45am Breakfast and Networking)
There has been a recent focus on women’s health, but there is more to gaps in care than hormone replacement therapies. At this session we’ll explore some common health issues where symptoms, diagnosis and treatments vary between genders, but where differences are not always recognized. Insurers, benefit advisors and plan sponsors should be aware of when symptoms and treatment for a man can be different than for a woman. It is important to take differences into account when designing benefit plans and administering claims, which is not always the case today. Speakers will be announced soon.
Agenda:The ROI of Time in Migraine Treatment: Gender differences in migraines and how timely access to preventative treatments can reclaim time for sponsors and employees.
Diagnosing and Treating Mental Health in Men and Women: While one in three Canadians will experience mental health issues in their lifetime, men are less likely to seek treatment and more likely to die from suicide. Learn how workplaces can be inclusive to the needs of both men and women’s mental health.
Cardiovascular Disease: Women are often undiagnosed or misdiagnosed. Many are unaware that signs and symptoms of a heart attack can differ between men and women. Our industry has an opportunity to educate and treat disease early, before disability or death.
The Golden Secret Behind Neurodiversity: How much do you know about neurodiversity as a workplace asset? With some minor accommodations those on the autism spectrum can provide a competitive edge in the workplace, but only if there is an accurate diagnosis, training and accommodations. Girls are less likely to display their autism symptoms compared to boys and therefore diagnosis can be delayed. This can have severe consequences leading to a heavier caregiver burden. Learn about key attributes of those on the spectrum, workplace accommodations that are easy to make, and the importance of employee training and HR policies.

column5: A performance of original compositions by Folias Duo, comprised of flautist Carmen Maret & Guitarist Andrew Bergeron.Show: 7:00-8:30 p.m.Doors: 6:30 p.m.Tickets: Pay What You Can (Suggested $30 Donation/person)This facility is wheelchair accessible.https://www.foliasmusic.com/Instagram: @foliasduoFacebook: @foliasduoQuestions - contact: niagaraclassics@gmail.comInstagram: @classicsniagarahttps://sites.google.com/view/classicsniagara"Theirs is a music that transcends genre and that ultimately brands itself as Folias Duo music, full stop." –Textura on Heartdance 2023Folias Duo is a trailblazing composer–performer ensemble for flute and guitar, known for blending classical music with jazz, world music, and improvisation. Founded by flutist Carmen Maret and guitarist Andrew Bergeron, the duo has developed a singular artistic voice through two decades of collaboration, live performance, and original composition.Based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Folias Duo has independently booked and performed over 700 concerts across the U.S., South America, and Europe. Their performances span a wide range of venues—from chamber music series and libraries to art galleries, house concerts, and guitar societies. During the pandemic, they produced 40 livestream broadcasts, continuing their creative output when many ensembles paused.Their discography includes eight albums, with the most recent—Heartdance—described by Fanfare Magazine as "a life-enhancing experience." Earlier recordings, produced by Latin Grammy-nominated Sergei Kvitko for Blue Griffin Records, were followed by three albums on their own Folias Music label, recorded at Sono Luminus Studios with Grammy-winning engineer Daniel Shores and producer Dan Merceruio.Maret and Bergeron have composed and recorded over 70 original works for flute and guitar—more than any duo of their kind worldwide. Their instrumentation includes C flute, alto flute, bass flute, piccolo, and tambin, paired with nylon-string guitar, creating a richly expressive and distinctive sound palette. They have also collaborated with string quartets, orchestras, and folk ensembles. Bergeron's broader works include a symphony, a guitar concerto, and a forthcoming flute concerto premiering in November 2025.As dedicated educators, they co-direct the Folias Music School and serve on the faculty at Aquinas College and Grand Rapids Community College. Maret recently completed a one-year appointment at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music. She holds a Bachelor of Music from the University of Missouri–Kansas City Conservatory and a Master of Music from Michigan State University. Bergeron holds a Bachelor of Arts from Grand Valley State University and a Master of Music from Michigan State University.Folias Duo's artistry is deeply tied to their way of life. Their touring philosophy embraces intentional, small-venue performances and a sustainable, self-directed model grounded in camping, cooking, and DIY production—a holistic, independent artistic ecosystem dedicated to craftsmanship, community, and the natural world.

column5: Up to 40 participants. Please call  716-244-2074 if you have questions or to request additional times if event shows sold out.Imagine stepping into a warmly lit studio, the air filled with the faint scent of acrylic paints and fresh canvases. Laughter echoes softly as friends, colleagues, or family members gather around long tables draped in protective plastic sheets, each person claiming their spot - a blank canvas, and a palette of vibrant colors. This is the essence of a group canvas painting event—a communal celebration of artistry, where novices and seasoned painters alike come together to unleash their inner creativity under the guidance of an enthusiastic instructor. This event, often hosted as corporate team-building activities, transform ordinary evenings into memorable adventures in self-expression and collaboration.At its core, a group canvas painting event is designed to be accessible and fun, stripping away the intimidation often associated with fine art. Participants don't need prior experience; in fact, the beauty lies in the inclusivity. The session typically begins with a warm welcome from the host / instructor. They'll outline the evening's theme—perhaps a serene landscape like a sunset over rolling hills, a whimsical abstract design inspired by nature, or a seasonal motif such as blooming cherry blossoms in spring or cozy autumn leaves. Themes can be customized too: for a birthday party, it might be a personalized portrait of the guest of honor; for a corporate retreat, a motivational scene symbolizing teamwork, like interlocking gears forming a heart.As the group settles in, the instructor demonstrates the basics step by step. They'll start with sketching faint outlines on the canvas using light pencil marks or pre-printed guides for those who prefer structure. "First, we'll mix our base colors," the instructor might say, holding up a brush dipped in cerulean blue and cadmium yellow to create a lush green for foliage. Participants follow along, their brushes dipping into paint pots arranged neatly on shared trays—primaries like red, blue, and yellow, alongside earthy tones, metallics for flair, and plenty of white for blending. The room buzzes with energy as people experiment: one might accidentally splatter paint, turning a mistake into a "happy accident" à la Bob Ross, while another meticulously layers shades for depth.What sets a group canvas painting event apart from solitary painting is the social dynamic. It's not just about the artwork; it's about the connections forged through shared laughter and encouragement. Strangers become friends as they peek at each other's canvases, offering compliments like, "I love how you added those golden highlights to the sun!" or tips such as, "Try thinning the paint with a bit of water for a watercolor effect." For couples on a date night, it becomes a romantic escapade, painting side by side and perhaps collaborating on a diptych—two canvases that form one complete image when placed together. Families use it as bonding time, with kids giggling over exaggerated features in a family portrait, while parents appreciate the mess-free setup (all supplies provided, no cleanup required at home).The event's structure ensures a relaxed pace, usually spanning one, or two   hours. Some events incorporate games, like "paint roulette" or musical charis where participants swap canvases mid-way, adding an element of surprise and hilarity as they adapt to someone else's style.Beyond the fun, these events offer tangible benefits. Creatively, they boost confidence; many leave amazed at their own abilities, clutching a framed-worthy piece to hang at home. Psychologically, painting in a group setting promotes mindfulness, reducing stress as brushes glide across canvas, focusing minds on the present. For teams, it's an excellent team-builder, fostering communication and problem-solving—deciding how to blend colors or compose elements mirrors workplace collaboration. Studies from art therapy research even suggest such activities enhance emotional well-being, releasing endorphins similar to those from exercise.As the session winds down, the instructor circles the room, providing final tips on blending edges or adding highlights. Participants step back to admire their work, often posing for group photos with their masterpieces held high.In today's fast-paced world, a group canvas painting event stands as a refreshing antidote to digital overload—a hands-on, analog experience that reconnects people with their creative sides and each other. Whether it's a bachelorette party bursting with vibrant florals, a holiday gathering painting winter wonderlands, or a quiet friends' night recreating famous artworks with a twist, these events create lasting memories and tangible souvenirs. If you're seeking a way to spark joy, build bonds, or simply try something new, stepping into one of these colorful gatherings promises an evening painted in hues of happiness and discovery.

column5:
The introductory workshop allows students to learn how to throw on a  potter's wheel and hand build your own mugWelcome to the captivating world of pottery! In this hands-on class, you will embark on a creative journey to make your own unique mug on a pottery wheel. Guided by experienced instructor, you will learn the art of wheel throwing and experience the joy of transforming a lump of clay into a functional masterpiece.

The class begins with an introduction to the pottery wheel and its various components. You'll become acquainted with the tools and materials used throughout the process, including different types of clay, glazes, and sculpting tools. The instructor will share their expertise, providing valuable insights and tips to help you achieve the best results.

Once you have a solid understanding of the pottery wheel, it's time to get your hands dirty! You'll be given a block of clay and shown how to properly center and prepare it on the wheel. As you start spinning the wheel, you'll feel the clay respond to your touch, gradually taking shape beneath your fingertips.

Under the guidance of the instructor, you will learn essential techniques such as pulling, shaping, and thinning the clay walls to create the desired form of your mug. The process requires focus, patience, and a willingness to experiment. As you refine your skills, you'll gain confidence in controlling the clay's movement and shape.

Once you've molded the basic structure of your mug, it's time to add personal touches and details. You can get creative with handles, textures, and decorative elements to make your mug truly one-of-a-kind. The instructor will provide suggestions and support as you explore different design options, encouraging you to unleash your imagination.

After completing the shaping and decoration, your mug will need to dry and undergo the initial firing process. This ensures that it holds its form and is ready for glazing. Once the pieces are dry you'll have an option to book a subsequent session for $10, where you'll learn about glazes and different coloring techniques, allowing you to add vibrant or subtle hues to your creation.

Once the glazing is complete, your mug will be fired again in a kiln, bringing out the vibrant colors and transforming the raw clay into a durable, functional piece of art. Finally, it's time to behold your masterpiece and take it home with you, ready to be enjoyed with every sip of your favorite beverage.

Participating in a "Make Your Own Mug on Pottery Wheel" class not only provides a fantastic opportunity to explore your creativity but also offers a therapeutic experience that allows you to disconnect from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Whether you're a complete beginner or have some prior experience, this class promises to be an enriching and rewarding journey into the world of pottery. So roll up your sleeves, embrace the tactile nature of clay, and get ready to make a mug that will be treasured for years to come.

Come and enjoy the experience of tote painting. You will be guided step by step to learn how to paint on tote from start to finishThe paint on tote  class involves the application of paint on a cotton tote to create decorative or artistic designs. The class focuses on exploring different painting techniques and styles that can be used to enhance the natural beauty of the tote.
Here is a description of what the class may cover:
Introduction to Totes: The class begins with an introduction to totes as an art medium. Students learn about the characteristics of totes, such as the grain patterns, texture, and natural color variations, which can influence the painting process.
Preparation and Priming: Students are taught how to prepare the tote for painting. This may include applying a primer to improve paint adhesion and prevent bleeding.
Color Theory and Design: The class covers the fundamentals of color theory and design principles as they apply to painting on totes. Students learn about color mixing, shading, blending, and composition to create visually appealing artwork.
Painting Techniques: Various painting techniques specific to totes are explored. This may include brush techniques, stippling, dry brushing, glazing, and layering to achieve different effects and textures on the cotton.
Subject Matter and Themes: Students are encouraged to experiment with different subject matters and themes for their tote paintings. This may range from nature-inspired motifs like landscapes, flowers, and animals to abstract or contemporary designs.
Finishing and Sealing: Once the painting is complete, the class covers techniques for finishing and sealing the artwork to protect it and enhance its longevity. This may involve applying a varnish,  or sealant to preserve the paint and highlight the natural beauty of the tote.
Display and Presentation: The class concludes with discussions on how to display and present the finished totes. Students learn about framing options, mounting techniques, and ways to showcase their artwork in various settings.
Throughout the class, students receive guidance from the instructor, who provides demonstrations, critiques, and individualized feedback to help them improve their painting skills. The aim is to foster creativity and encourage students to explore the unique possibilities offered by painting on totes.
